# 1. Overview

Market Area Analysis is all about figuring out where your customers come from and what makes that area tick. Businesses analyze local demographics, consumer spending habits, and nearby competition to decide where to open, how to market, and when to expand. It combines practical observations—like asking shoppers for their ZIP codes—with mathematical models to map out foot traffic and shopping behavior.

One of the most popular tools used in this process is the Huff Model. It calculates the odds that someone will choose your store over a competitor's by weighing two main factors: how appealing your store is (size, selection, or brand pull) versus how far they have to travel to get there. As distance and competing options increase, the likelihood of a visit drops. Ultimately, the model helps retailers project revenue, map trade boundaries, and pick the best storefront locations.

## Business setting

In a fast-food franchise model, an independent operator (the franchisee) licenses the right to run a restaurant under a franchisor’s established brand, committing to standard operating guidelines and ongoing franchise fees. Key investment factors include brand equity, strategic location, and upfront capital, which typically ranges from \$200,000 to over \$2 million across major chains such as McDonald’s, KFC, Burger King, Pizza Hut, and Taco Bell.

Acting as a business development data analyst for a fast-food franchise, your task is to map and define the commercial trade areas of existing locations across Taichung City, generating spatial visualizations to drive strategic planning and market analysis.

## The data

Four data sets will be used in this hands-on exercise, they are:

Geospatial data

STORES_TN, store locations data in ESRI shapefile format. VILLAGE_TN, village boundary data in ESRI shapefile format. Aspatial data

pop2019.csv, population data of Taichung City in 2019. H_CNT, P_CNT, M_CNT, and F_CNT indicate Number of household, Total population, Male population and Female population respectively. Store_sales_data.csv provides store sales data, and

## The tools

In this exercise, we use below R package to do analysis.

- sf for handling geospatial data and performing geoprocessing function such as computing distance matrix,

- MCI for performing Huff and MCI modelling,

- tidyverse for performing data science tasks including visualisation,

- ggstatsplot, an R package that extends the ggplot2 visualization package to combine data visualization with statistical analysis, creating plots that include statistical test results directly, and

- tmap for plotting cartographic quality thematic maps.

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, MCI, tmap, ggstatsplot)
```

# 2. Data preparation 

# 2.1 Importing geospatial data

Import Tai Chung store data

```{r}
stores <- st_read(
  dsn = "data/geospatial",
  layer = "STORES_TC")
```

Import town geospatial data

```{r}
town <- st_read(
  dsn = "data/geospatial",
  layer = "TOWN_TC") 
```

Import village geospatial data

```{r}
village <- st_read(
  dsn = "data/geospatial",
  layer = "VILLAGE_TC")

```

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(town) +
  tm_polygons() +
  tm_shape(village) +
  tm_polygons() + 
  tm_shape(stores) +
  tm_dots()
```

```{r}
tmap_mode("plot")
```

## 2.2 Importing asspatial data

Importing population data and store data

```{r}
pop2019 <- read_csv("data/aspatial/pop2019.csv")

store_sales <- read_csv("data/aspatial/Store_sales_data.csv")
```

Verify store data

```{r}
summary(store_sales)
```

## 2.3 Data preparation

### 2.3.1 Aggregating store sales

```{r}
store_sales_aggre <- store_sales %>%
  group_by(`Store Code`) %>%
  summarise(
    "Total_Bill" = sum(Bills, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Total_Sales" = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### 2.3.2 Relational join

```{r}
stores <- stores %>%
  left_join(store_sales_aggre,
            by = join_by(
              Store_CD == `Store Code`)) %>%
  mutate(Store_size = 100)
```

```{r}
summary(stores)
```

### 2.3.3 Tidying pop2019 data

Before joining `pop2019` with the `village` `sf` layer, it is best practice to verify that the common identifier fields contain identical values.

```{r}
glimpse(pop2019)
```

```{r}
glimpse(village)
```

The plot above shown that the village ID (i.e. V_ID) in pop2019 data.frame is not in the same structure as the village code in village sf data.frame.

we need to remove "-" in V_ID

```{r}
pop2019 <- pop2019 %>%
  mutate(V_ID = str_remove_all(
    V_ID, "-"))
```

Now, we are ready to append data in pop2019 data.frame onto village sf data.frame by using left_join() of dplyr package.

```{r}
village <- village %>%
  left_join(pop2019,
            by = join_by(
              VILLCODE == V_ID))
```

### 2.3.4 Check for missing or zero values

```{r}
summary(village)
```

There are five missing values in H_CNT, P_CNT, M_CNT and F_CNT fields.

Hence, code chunk below is used to remove the five records with missing values from village sf data.frame.

```{r}
village <- village %>%
  filter(!is.na(P_CNT)) 
```

```{r}
any(is.na(village$H_CNT))
```

```{r}
any(is.na(village$P_CNT))
```

```{r}
any(is.na(village$M_CNT))
```

```{r}
any(is.na(village$F_CNT))
```

# 3. Computing Distance Matrix

Instead of calculate the distance between the villages and stores, we will calculate the centroid of each village using the code chunk below. Then, compute the distance between the centroids of the villages and the stores.

```{r}
village_center <- st_point_on_surface(village)
distmat <- st_distance(village_center, stores) 
```

Next, the code chunk below is used to convert the distance matrix into long data.frame format

```{r}
rownames(distmat) <- village$`VILLCODE`
colnames(distmat) <- stores$`Store_CD`

distmat_long <- distmat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "VILLCODE") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -VILLCODE,
    names_to = "Store_CD",
    values_to = "distance"
  ) %>%
  mutate(distance = as.numeric(distance)) 
```

# 4. Preparing Interaction Matrix

Build the interaction matrix required by MCI package.

```{r}
interaction_matrix <- distmat_long %>%
  left_join(
    stores %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      select(Store_CD, Store_size),
    by = "Store_CD") %>%
  relocate(
    distance, .after = last_col())
```

```{r}
summary(interaction_matrix)
```

# 5. Computing Huff model

```{r}
huff_share <- huff.shares(
  interaction_matrix, "VILLCODE", "Store_CD", 
  "Store_size", "distance")
```

## 5.1 Trade area analysis for a single store

select market share data of a store by using *Store_CD* field (i.e. TG).

```{r}
market_share <- huff_share %>%
  filter(Store_CD == "BT")
```

Next, trade areas of the selected will be derived by using the code chun below.

```{r}
Trade_area <- village %>%
  left_join(market_share)
```

Before plotting the trade area map, code chunk below is used to extract the selected store from stores sf data.frame.

```{r}
selected_store <- stores %>%
  filter(Store_CD == "BT")
```

plot the trade areas of the selected store.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 10
tm_shape(Trade_area) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "p_ij",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile", 
                n = 10,
                values = "brewer.blues"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(
                title = "Patronage Probability")) +
  tm_shape(selected_store) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Distribution of Patronage Probability of Store BT by village") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha =0.2) 
```

## 5.2 Store sales analysis

One of the usage of Huff model is to estimate the store sales by using village population.

Firstly, let us append P_CNT field from *village* sf.data.frame to *huff_share* data.frame by using the code chunk below.

```{r}
huff_share_pp <- huff_share %>%
  left_join(village %>% 
              st_drop_geometry() %>% 
              select(VILLCODE, P_CNT),
            by = "VILLCODE") %>%
  relocate(
    distance, .after = last_col())
```

calculate the total sales

```{r}
huff_total <- shares.total(
  huff_share_pp, "VILLCODE", "Store_CD",
  "p_ij", "P_CNT")
```

append the estimate store sales (Ej) onto stores sf data.frame.

```{r}
store_sales_est <- stores %>%
  left_join(huff_total,
            by = join_by(
              "Store_CD" == "suppliers_single"))
```

visualise how well the estimate sales as compare to the actual sales

```{r}
store_sales_nongeom <- store_sales_est %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()

ggscatterstats(
  store_sales_nongeom,
  x = sum_E_j,
  y = Total_Sales)
```

```{r}
huff_share_wider <- huff_share %>%
  select(VILLCODE, Store_CD, p_ij) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Store_CD, 
              values_from = p_ij)
```

```{r}
summary(huff_share_wider) 
```
